title: Program Kit generated Console command dispatch
intent: Add one deterministic generated-host dispatch seam that hands a successful Open Console parse to consumer-owned code and returns the consumer's exact integer exit code without changing parser bytes, importing consumer semantics, or adding a Program Kit generator runtime dependency.
scope: A generated internal IProgramKitConsoleCommandDispatcher contract in the generated host assembly whose DispatchAsync method receives the unchanged GeneratedConsoleParseResult and a host application-stopping CancellationToken and returns ValueTask<int>.
A consumer-owned partial Program composition hook for explicit IServiceCollection registration of the dispatcher and ordinary consumer services.

Successful-command startup that composes the configured host, resolves the required dispatcher before hosted behavior starts, starts the host, dispatches exactly once, stops the host in a finally path, and returns the dispatcher's integer unchanged.
Preservation of existing parse-failure, help, and completion behavior without requiring dispatcher registration or host startup.

Exact Open Console document revision propagation into generation input plus deterministic console-dispatch lock and evidence projections that bind document, generator, dispatch-contract, parser, parse-result, registration, and lifecycle facts.
Compiler, unit, conformance, isolated-consumer, source-gate, deterministic-generation, lock, evidence, package, and process-exit verification.
nonGoals: No JTest domain types, run-evidence model, test semantics, repository code, or consumer-specific command implementation.
No change to GeneratedConsoleParser.cs or GeneratedConsoleParseResult.cs bytes for an unchanged Open Console input.
No runtime dependency from a generated application to Orbyss.ProgramKit.DotNet, Workbench, CommandLine, Development, Planning, or a new Program Kit runtime dispatcher package.
No reflection, assembly scanning, static behavioral collaborator, ambient dispatcher, hook, watcher, MCP binding, tool binding, provider binding, or autonomous dispatch.
No Program Kit-owned mapping from exceptions, cancellation, or arbitrary consumer results to JTest's exit codes.
No Open Console grammar, option, argument, help, completion, stream, or exit-code schema redesign.
No base-CShells-optional shell contract or dotnet-shell v12 migration.
assumptions: Consumer-owned dispatcher and composition source is compiled into the generated host assembly beside the isolated ProgramKitGenerated tree, as with the existing generated FastEndpoints dispatcher port.
An internal generated dispatcher interface may reference the existing internal GeneratedConsoleParseResult without changing parser/result accessibility or requiring a new runtime package.
The existing internal static partial Program type is the correct explicit composition boundary for one optional consumer-authored service-registration method.

A successful command is a one-shot host operation: configured hosted behavior starts before dispatch, a long-running command may await cancellation inside the dispatcher, and the host stops after dispatch completes or fails.
The consumer dispatcher returns only exit codes meaningful under its accepted Open Console declaration; Program Kit preserves the integer unchanged and does not clamp it.
The current dotnet-shell v11 contract permits empty featureActivationIdentities even though it requires one shell identity and the base CShells 0.0.28 package.
The artifact manifest remains the authority for the exact Open Console document revision and the artifact resolver continues to verify its bytes before generation.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the generated Console dispatcher, lifecycle, integrity, compatibility, and consumer-ownership boundaries as a validated canonical design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design carries architecture meaning and grants no runtime behavior.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The design is schema-validated, reviewed at exact bytes, digest-bound by its plan, and compared during implementation closure.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The repository artifact is explicit input and is not discovered through an agent retrieval system.

agentProcedure.rationale: The design does not define, register, or authorize an agent capability.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit architecture reviewer, implementer, and blocked Console-host consumers.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only an explicit human decision over the exact design and implementation-plan digests may approve implementation.
humanCommunication.rationale: A reviewer-oriented Markdown projection and exact review manifest expose lifecycle, compatibility, and failure behavior.

generatedNavigation.rationale: No generated navigation artifact is required for this bounded review set.

governance.provenancePolicy: The exact human intent, current Program Kit source commit and bytes, Open Console schema, and C# source gate are named; later implementation cannot become retroactive design authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest and plan bind exact canonical design bytes; changes require revalidation, new digests, and renewed human decision.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Any generated dispatcher signature, parser bytes, registration hook, lifecycle order, lock/evidence schema, exit-code pass-through, package boundary, or shell constraint change requires explicit compatibility review and a new design version.
governance.migrationPolicy: Implementation must version changed lock or generation-input contracts explicitly, update schemas and fixtures together, and retain a byte-stability regression for existing parser outputs.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: No consumer arguments, option values, test evidence, credentials, secrets, personal data, or runtime output is included.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Only the repository review set and its validated human-readable projections are intended externalizations.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Runtime command values, process output, services, host state, and cancellation state remain outside the canonical design.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A schema-governed design instance is the canonical authority for the bounded Console dispatch extension while implementation remains blocked pending exact human approval.

security.policy: The generated seam transports an already validated parse to registered consumer behavior and adds no identity, authorization, credential, or secret meaning.
guarantees: Command, option, and argument validation remains owned by the accepted generated parser.
No service or dispatcher is discovered from unreviewed assemblies.
exclusions: The dispatcher result is not an authorization decision or security status.

authority.policy: The consumer explicitly authors and registers command behavior; Program Kit only generates the transport and lifecycle seam.
guarantees: A successful parse does not grant command authority beyond consumer-owned implementation.
exclusions: No automatic registration, reflection discovery, or inferred command handler is allowed.

secrets.policy: Locks and evidence record revisions, paths, digests, and contract facts only.
guarantees: Argument and option values are not copied into durable lock or evidence artifacts.
exclusions: No runtime command input, environment value, credential, or secret becomes generation evidence.

persistence.policy: Only deterministic generated source, lock, documentation, and bounded evidence are durable.
guarantees: Host runtime state and dispatcher service state remain process-local.
exclusions: The seam owns no command-result store, execution journal, queue, or retry state.

failure.policy: Parser failures preserve declared parser codes; missing registration fails before host start; successful dispatch returns the consumer integer unchanged.
guarantees: No parsed command silently succeeds without consumer behavior.
Host stop is attempted after dispatch completion, cancellation, or exception.
Program Kit does not rewrite a consumer return value.
exclusions: Program Kit does not define a universal exception-to-exit-code mapping.

concurrency.policy: One process invocation dispatches one successful parse exactly once.
guarantees: The generated host creates no shared mutable dispatcher registry or background dispatch loop.
exclusions: Parallel command execution, retries, batching, and cross-process coordination are consumer concerns.

cancellation.policy: The dispatcher receives the configured host's application-stopping token and owns semantic cancellation handling.
guarantees: Host shutdown is attempted in a bounded finally path after dispatch leaves.
exclusions: Cancellation does not imply rollback of consumer side effects or a Program Kit-owned exit code.

observability.policy: Generation evidence describes exact revisions and output integrity without observing consumer command data.
guarantees: Tests observe process exit codes, dispatch count, lifecycle order, missing registration, and deterministic bytes.
exclusions: No command input, domain evidence, stdout/stderr payload, exception payload, or personal data is retained as lock evidence.

compatibility.policy: The generated source contract, lock/evidence schemas, input revision binding, shell constraint, and parser-byte baseline version independently and fail closed on drift.
guarantees: Existing parser and parse-result bytes remain stable for unchanged input.
Generated applications retain no Program Kit generator runtime dependency.
An empty feature-activation selection requires no CShells feature package.
exclusions: The base CShells 0.0.28 package and one shell identity remain required by dotnet-shell v11.

scenarios.intent: Execute a successfully parsed command through consumer-owned services and expose its declared result as the process exit code.
preconditions: The Open Console document and shell bytes match their exact artifact revisions.
Consumer source implements and registers the generated dispatcher port.
steps: Parse arguments with the unchanged generated parser.
Create the configured host builder and invoke the consumer registration partial method.
Build the host and resolve the required dispatcher before host start.
Start the host, dispatch the exact parse once with the application-stopping token, and capture the integer result.
Stop the host in a finally path and return the captured integer.
outcomes: The process exit code equals the dispatcher's returned integer.
Consumer services are resolved through constructor injection from explicit composition-root registrations.
Identical generation input produces identical output bytes.
failureOutcomes: Missing dispatcher registration fails before hosted behavior starts.
Consumer exceptions are not misreported as generated success.

scenarios.intent: Receive declared parse diagnostics, help, or completion without requiring consumer command composition.
preconditions: The generated parser accepts the exact Open Console document.
steps: For parse failure, write the diagnostic to stderr and return its declared exit code.
For help or completion, write the information output to stdout and return its declared exit code.
outcomes: Existing parse and information behavior remains byte- and process-compatible.
The dispatcher and host are not resolved or started.
failureOutcomes: No nondispatch path may fall through to a silent generated return of zero.

scenarios.intent: Bind one Console dispatch seam to exact source documents and prove deterministic regeneration.
preconditions: The artifact manifest binds the Console host to one exact Open Console document revision.
steps: Verify shell and document bytes against their declared revisions.
Generate parser, parse result, dispatcher port, composition, lock, evidence, and documentation in ordinal path order.
Regenerate from the same inputs and compare every output path and byte.
Change the document or dispatcher contract revision and verify the corresponding lock/evidence digest changes.
outcomes: The lock and evidence name the exact document, generator, dispatcher contract, and generated contract paths.
The parser and parse-result baseline digests remain unchanged for unchanged input.
failureOutcomes: Missing, stale, mismatched, or nondeterministic revision evidence fails generation or conformance.

statusClaims.claim: The Console dispatch design review set is being produced from explicit human intent; none of the described runtime source, lock/evidence contracts, migrations, or conformance fixtures is implemented or approved by this claim.
